name: resolution-and-reliability-20261107
status: Exploratory follow-up on previously inspected screens; declared before computing the new endpoints. This does not replace the failed NCATS confirmation.

experiment_1.hypothesis: Similar dose-response error can conceal material differences in pair-cell mean and pair-specific contrast error among neural, GP and CF methods.
experiment_1.primary: Paired relative contrast MSE: GP F2 versus neural F2, CF selected versus neural F0, GP F0 versus neural F0. Holm-adjusted delete-one-drug tests across these three comparisons.
levels: pair-cell mean, both equal-panel and dose-row weights
residuals against training-pair Bliss and HSA
pair-cell interaction contrast and within-panel dose-shape contrast
experiment_1.decomposition: Weighted orthogonal sums of squares: grand mean; additive drug effects within cell and outer fold on pair-cell means; remaining pair-cell contrast; within-panel additive drug-dose-rank effects within cell and fold; remaining within-panel dose shape; replicate deviations at identical inputs. Every component uses the same projector for truth and prediction. This is an evaluation contrast, not a fitted predictor or a causal interaction estimate.
experiment_1.new_information_ablations: If compute is accessible, use the production neural architecture and fixed training settings with drug identity, cell identity, dose, or monotherapy removed separately; no architecture search. Preserve monotherapy lookup identities internally while masking only model inputs. Five outer folds, seeds 2026/2027/2028. Existing model families are compared only within their documented input regimes; CF has no native monotherapy feature interface.
experiment_1.inference: Whole-pair bootstrap, delete-one-drug jackknife with contrast projections refitted after each deletion, and fold/seed consistency. Conditional pair bootstrap on projected scores is labelled conditional. No dose-row iid intervals. Report equal-weight pair-cell sensitivity and replicate-noise estimates.
experiment_1.decision: Material superiority requires at least 5% contrast-MSE reduction, Holm p<0.05, both grouped intervals excluding zero and the same direction in all five folds. Response equivalence requires both grouped 95% intervals entirely within +/-5% relative MSE. Otherwise describe uncertainty without equivalence/superiority claims.
experiment_1.negative_result: Failure to distinguish models limits evidence for interaction-specific advantages; high response R2 alone is insufficient.

experiment_2.hypothesis: Replacing only numerically rejected admissible Loewe roots changes experimental prioritization, while near-boundary and fit uncertainty may limit the stability of either ranking.
experiment_2.primary: Retention of the native top 5% pair-cell combinations after the valid_root_any correction; secondary top 1%/10%, within-cell top 5%, pair averages, sign flips, rank correlation and rank displacement.
controls: original fixed coefficients and historical native results
experiment_2.perturbations: First test fixed-coefficient numerical rounding to 6/8/10 significant digits and multiplicative dose changes +/-1e-6. Then native drc single-agent refits at unchanged data and parametric response perturbations: 0.1, 0.5, 1 and 2 inhibition points, plus a repeat-grounded scale only if independent monotherapy repeats can be established. Treat shared copied edges as one curve, not independent replicates. Seeded fixed curve sample stratified by fallback and boundary status; selection uses historical status, never new ranking outcomes.
experiment_2.acceptance_rules: Compare historical termination-code rule, native answer accepted only when strictly in both effect ranges and absolute equation residual <1e-6, and independent bracketed roots with that same certificate. Sensitivity residual thresholds 1e-4 and 1e-8. Do not certify opposite-direction/no-root cases or change clipping/fallback definitions.
experiment_2.inference: Whole-drug-pair bootstrap for ranking overlap; delete-one-drug sensitivity. Native refits are a paired numerical experiment, not independent biological evidence.
experiment_2.decision: A material prioritization effect requires at least 5% turnover of the top-5% list and a pair-bootstrap lower bound above zero turnover. Report whether this persists within cells and whether perturbation turnover is larger. Rank change is not proof the corrected ranking predicts biological efficacy better.
experiment_2.negative_result: Stable ranks would restrict the consequence to score reconstruction/calibration. Fit sensitivity would weaken prioritization claims even if fixed-fit numerical correction is verified.

experiment_3.hypothesis: Dose, monotherapy coverage and response-distribution differences explain part of the heterogeneous within-screen gains.
experiment_3.primary: Change in the between-screen F2-versus-Bliss relative MSE-gain difference after standardizing common input-defined strata: Bliss level, log-dose range and monotherapy availability.
experiment_3.controls: Exact drug/cell mappings and units first; no guessed aliases. Report common-support mass, sample sizes and effective sample sizes. Prior NCATS H1 failures remain failed. Compare response conventions and shared monotherapy provenance before interpreting standardized differences.
experiment_3.transfer_gate: Frozen source models may be tested only on identified shared drugs/cells with source-supported doses and compatible response definitions. If these gates fail, report the overlap audit and do not interpret transport as biological generalization. A monotherapy-only calibration function is an exploratory transport control where identities do not overlap.
experiment_3.decision: Describe a measurable contribution only when the standardized gap is smaller with a grouped interval supporting the reduction; this is descriptive, not causal attribution. No new screen search.
experiment_3.negative_result: Persistent heterogeneity or poor overlap rules out simple transport claims and motivates a harmonized repeated assay.

experiment_4.hypothesis: GP uncertainty or neural disagreement improves combination-level error detection beyond validation-calibrated cell and dose/monotherapy baselines.
experiment_4.primary: Pair-cell mean squared error captured by the highest-uncertainty 10% of pair-cell units; paired difference versus the strongest validation-only simple baseline. Secondary 90% coverage, Gaussian NLL, risk-coverage and ranking correlation.
experiment_4.controls: GP predictive versus latent SD; neural ensemble mean and three-seed disagreement, with validation-fitted noise floor/scale; validation RMSE global/per-cell and monotone error model based on dose and monotherapy; empirical replicate dispersion where estimable. Restore validation predictions from existing checkpoints where necessary; no test-error calibration.
experiment_4.inference: Whole-pair bootstrap and delete-one-drug intervals. Treat the ensemble as an ensemble, separately from the historical seed-average metrics. Selecting high-error combinations is a measurement-planning surrogate, not demonstrated experimental utility.
experiment_4.decision: Useful error triage requires at least a 5-percentage-point increase in error mass captured at 10% budget with both grouped intervals above zero. Calibration alone does not establish useful ranking.
experiment_4.negative_result: If simple baselines match uncertainty, recommend those baselines; disagreement without observation noise is not a predictive interval.
